articles.excerpt: I've been quietly building Antigravity Tools — a collection of 59 free, browser-based developer utilities — and today I'm sharing everything I built and learned. The main constraint I set for myself:…
articles.body: I've been quietly building Antigravity Tools — a collection of 59 free, browser-based developer utilities — and today I'm sharing everything I built and learned. Why vanilla JS? No React, no build step. The main constraint I set for myself: zero dependencies, zero server, zero telemetry . When you paste your JWT token into jwt.io, it goes to their server. When you use an online regex tester, your test strings are logged. I built Antigravity Tools so every operation runs inside your browser, using native APIs. No Node.js backend No npm packages No webpack/vite/parcel No Google Analytics No cookies Everything runs on Web Crypto API , Canvas API , Web Audio API , and IndexedDB — all native to modern browsers.

articles.body: If you are building a Dubai PropTech app, an Automated Valuation Model (AVM), or a yield-screening pipeline in Python, one of your first searches is probably bayut api . Here is the short engineering reality: Bayut does not offer a public, self-serve REST API for querying market listings. Official XML and CRM feeds exist for licensed UAE brokerages, and those integrations are designed to push an agency's own inventory into the portal rather than export market-wide search datasets. For independent data engineers and automation builders, UAE property data lives in three disconnected places: Portal XML/CRM Partner Feeds: Restricted to registered brokerages managing their own active stock.

articles.title: Reading a cutting list from a photo with an LLM, without trusting the model
articles.excerpt: A glazier gets a photo of a handwritten sheet: "V1 1200 x 800, 2 uds", a crossed-out line, a phone number. A vision model can read that. The trouble is what happens when it reads it wrong and the numb…
articles.body: A glazier gets a photo of a handwritten sheet: "V1 1200 x 800, 2 uds", a crossed-out line, a phone number. A vision model can read that. The trouble is what happens when it reads it wrong and the numbers go straight into a machine that cuts expensive glass. A 1200 mistaken for 1700 is not a typo, it is a pane in the bin. This is how the endpoint behind the "read the list from a photo or PDF" option of SyntaxFlow is built ( functions/api/list-ai.js , a Cloudflare Pages Function). The design assumption is in one sentence of its header: the model's word is not trusted. Principle: the model transcribes, the code decides The model never decides what goes into the list. It returns candidate rows.

articles.title: 12 grains of dust found high in Earth's atmosphere reveal secrets of water at the edge of the solar system
articles.excerpt: Grains of dust found floating in Earth's stratosphere hold the secrets of a special kind of 'heavy' water that seems to be abundant in the outer solar system.
articles.body: A dozen grains of dust that have wandered in from the distant Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune were found floating in Earth's stratosphere. And it turns out they hold the secrets of a special kind of 'heavy' water that seems to be surprisingly abundant in the outer solar system. When analyzed by a team of scientists the 12 dust grains, which were captured by NASA's stratospheric ER-2 research aircraft, show signs of having interacted with a form of water that contains heavy oxygen isotopes. This is important because to better understand how the planets formed, scientists are seeking to understand how various materials were distributed around the early solar system 4.5 billion years ago.

articles.excerpt: Atmos Space Cargo will fly its first Phoenix cargo-return capsule on SpaceX's Bandwagon 3 rideshare mission, which is scheduled to launch this spring.
articles.body: A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration.
